title: Making Good Decisions About Strategy
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article proposes that the strongest predictor of a good strategic decision is whether the leader has first shaped a coherent story of the future before evaluating specific options. It describes how this narrative — with characters, motivations, actions, and a conclusion — gives leaders a framework for assessing how a given strategy would actually play out, including likely competitor reactions and points of resistance. The piece frames storytelling not as a soft communication add-on but as a genuine decision-making tool that should be made explicit before a strategic choice is finalized.
points: Research cited in the piece finds the best predictor of a quality strategic decision is whether the leader shaped a story of the future before evaluating options.
This storyline includes key actors, motivations, a sequence of events, and an implied lesson or conclusion.
Making the storyline explicit strengthens its power to guide the ultimate strategic choice.
The narrative helps leaders anticipate competitor reactions, execution roadblocks, and team capability gaps.
The article frames storytelling as a genuine decision-making tool, not just a communication device.
quotes: Research confirms that the leader and how they think about the future remain the most crucial components regarding the quality of a decision about strategy.
As it turns out, the best predictor of such a quality decision is whether a leader shapes a story about the future before they consider each option.
Like all good stories, this storyline includes key actors, their motivations, a set of actions and judgments that develop the narrative, and a conclusion with a lesson.
Stories are powerful organizing structures that enhance decision-making when they are deployed effectively.
Sound strategy starts with having a clear storyline that articulates a leader’s personal vision for the future.
